definitions.explanation: A detailed plan prepared by a teacher outlining the objectives, content, methods, and activities for a class session or series of lessons.

examples.japanese: {授業案|じゅぎょうあん}を{作成|さくせい}する。
{明日|あした}の{授業案|じゅぎょうあん}をまだ{書|か}いていない。
examples.english: I haven't written tomorrow's lesson plan yet.

examples.japanese: {教育|きょういく}{実習|じっしゅう}では、{毎日|まいにち}{授業案|じゅぎょうあん}を{提出|ていしゅつ}しなければならなかった。
examples.english: During the teaching practicum, I had to submit a lesson plan every day.

notes:
Combines {授業|じゅぎょう} (class, lesson) and {案|あん} (plan, proposal). Essential vocabulary for anyone involved in education in Japan. Lesson plans are a formal part of teacher preparation and are particularly important during {教育|きょういく}{実習|じっしゅう} (teaching practice/student teaching).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {授業案|じゅぎょうあん}を{作|つく}る: to make a lesson plan
- {授業案|じゅぎょうあん}を{書|か}く: to write a lesson plan
- {授業案|じゅぎょうあん}を{提出|ていしゅつ}する: to submit a lesson plan
- {授業案|じゅぎょうあん}の{検討|けんとう}: review of a lesson plan

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {指導案|しどうあん}: instruction plan (more formal, used in official educational contexts)
- {学習|がくしゅう}{指導|しどう}{案|あん}: formal teaching guide/plan (official term used in Japanese education)
- カリキュラム: curriculum (broader scope than a single lesson plan)
